title: Walled gardens loosen clean-room rules for advertisers
summary: Two large ad platforms said advertisers can now export aggregated clean-room results into their own warehouses, with minimum audience thresholds of 1,000 users. Measurement teams have asked for this for years because it lets them blend platform lift studies with their own sales data. Privacy groups
body: Two large ad platforms said advertisers can now export aggregated clean-room results into their own warehouses, with minimum audience thresholds of 1,000 users. Measurement teams have asked for this for years because it lets them blend platform lift studies with their own sales data. Privacy groups say the thresholds are still too low to prevent re-identification.

title: Incrementality testing moves from quarterly project to always-on
summary: A survey of 212 brand-side analytics leads found 41% now run geo-based incrementality tests continuously rather than as one-off projects, up from 18% two years ago. body: A survey of 212 brand-side analytics leads found 41% now run geo-based incrementality tests continuously rather than as one-off projects, up from 18% two years ago. Teams cite cheaper holdout design tooling and pressure to defend retail media budgets. The main complaint is that test results arrive after the budget decision has already been made.

title: New open-source MMM library adds saturation curves with priors by channel
summary: A new release of an open-source Bayesian marketing mix model library lets analysts set channel-specific priors for saturation and carryover. body: A new release of an open-source Bayesian marketing mix model library lets analysts set channel-specific priors for saturation and carryover. Early users report that weakly informative priors cut the width of credible intervals for small channels by about a third. The maintainers warn that priors copied from another brand's results can bias estimates.

title: Retail media networks agree on a common reporting template
summary: Five retail media networks published a shared reporting template covering impressions, attributed sales windows and new-to-brand definitions. Advertisers have struggled to compare results across networks because each used a different attribution window, ranging from 7 to 30 days. The template is vol
body: Five retail media networks published a shared reporting template covering impressions, attributed sales windows and new-to-brand definitions. Advertisers have struggled to compare results across networks because each used a different attribution window, ranging from 7 to 30 days. The template is voluntary and does not yet cover in-store sales.

title: Retail media networks publish shared reporting template
summary: Five retail media networks released a common reporting template that standardises attribution windows and new-to-brand definitions. The template is optional and leaves out in-store sales.
body: Five retail media networks released a common reporting template that standardises attribution windows and new-to-brand definitions. The template is optional and leaves out in-store sales.

title: Brands cut branded search spend after lift test shows little incremental sales
summary: A packaged-goods brand paused branded search in four test markets and saw total sales fall by under 1%, far less than the platform-reported conversions suggested. The team reallocated the saved budget to retail media. Analysts caution that results depend on how strong the brand's organic listing is
body: A packaged-goods brand paused branded search in four test markets and saw total sales fall by under 1%, far less than the platform-reported conversions suggested. The team reallocated the saved budget to retail media. Analysts caution that results depend on how strong the brand's organic listing is and how many competitors bid on its name.

title: Consent rates fall as more browsers prompt by default
summary: Average opt-in rates on consent banners dropped from 62% to 54% over six months in a panel of 90 European publishers. Modelled conversions now fill a larger share of reported results. Measurement vendors disagree on how to disclose the modelled share to advertisers.

body: In a study of 14 snack and beverage brands, creator posts accounted for 33% of social-attributed sales, with the strongest effect from creators who posted at least twice a week. The authors note that attribution relied on promo codes and link clicks, which undercount people who saw a post and bought in store later.

title: Why last-click reporting still wins budget meetings
summary: Finance teams keep asking for last-click numbers because they reconcile to invoices and are easy to audit. Analysts who present multi-touch or MMM results report better outcomes when they show both views side by side and explain the gap between them in one slide.
body: Finance teams keep asking for last-click numbers because they reconcile to invoices and are easy to audit. Analysts who present multi-touch or MMM results report better outcomes when they show both views side by side and explain the gap between them in one slide.

title: Forecasting tools add budget what-if scenarios to media plans
summary: Three planning platforms now let media buyers test what-if scenarios, such as moving 15% of spend from television to streaming, against a marketing mix model. Buyers like the speed, but some warn that scenarios outside the range of past spend are extrapolation, not prediction.

title: Panel data shows value shoppers trading down on multipacks
summary: Household panel data shows lower-income households bought 9% fewer single units and 4% more multipacks over the last quarter. Retailers are responding with price-per-unit labels. Brands that raised list prices lost more volume in these households than in others.
